alt: Table matching ten types of data to suitable presentation and statistics, from located proportional symbols for values at points to dispersion diagrams and standard deviation for the spread of one data set. A note says a justification needs what the technique shows and why it suits the data.

after: ## Core skills: annotation, literacy and numeracy
alt: Two bars to scale: a town of 48,000 grows to 61,200, an increase of 13,200 shown in gold. Formulas below: percentage change = 13,200 / 48,000 x 100 = 27.5%, and mean rate of change over 12 years = 1,100 people a year.
caption: Percentage change compares with the starting value; rate of change divides by time.

alt: Points A (140) and B (190) lie 25 mm apart on a scale bar. The 160 isoline crosses 10 mm from A, because 160 is 0.4 of the way from 140 to 190. Steps show the calculation and the assumption that values change evenly between points.
caption: Find the fraction of the value gap, then take that fraction of the distance.

alt: Three circles drawn to scale: 2,500 visitors with a radius of 8 mm, 6,400 visitors with 12.8 mm and 10,000 visitors with 16 mm, showing that four times the value doubles the radius. Below, a flow line 7.5 mm wide for 3,750 vehicles a day at 1 mm per 500 vehicles.
caption: Scale circle area, not radius, to the value; scale flow-line width to volume.

alt: A triangular graph with corners at 100% clay, 100% silt and 100% sand and gridlines every 10%. Dashed lines at 20% clay, 30% silt and 50% sand meet at a single plotted point. Notes say to check the three values add to 100% and that clustered points show similar samples.
caption: Check the three values total 100%, then plot where the three gridlines meet.

alt: Dispersion diagram of two sets of seven infiltration times with the same mean of 22 seconds. Set A clusters between 18 and 26 seconds with a standard deviation of 2.4 s; set B spreads from 8 to 36 seconds with 9.6 s. Shaded bands show one standard deviation either side of the mean.
caption: The same mean can hide very different spread: report both.

after: ## Statistical skills: interpreting spread and testing relationships
alt: Scatter graph of eight invented sites: recorded crimes fall from 42 at 0.2 km to 15 at 3.7 km from the centre. The calculation gives rs = -0.952; on a scale from 0 to 1 its size lies beyond the critical values 0.738 (0.05) and 0.881 (0.01), so the null hypothesis is rejected at the 0.01 level.
caption: A strong negative correlation, significant at 0.01, but it does not prove cause.

alt: Paired bars compare observed and expected counts: within 200 m of the river 34 aware and 16 not aware against expected 27.5 and 22.5; over 200 m 21 and 29 against the same expected values. Chi-square = 6.83 with 1 degree of freedom, beyond the critical values 3.84 and 6.63, so the difference is significant at the 0.01 level.
caption: Observed counts differ from expected enough to be significant at 0.01.
